title: Build a singly linked list in Rust — 3 turns
description: Three turns build a singly linked list in Rust: turn 1 push_front/pop_front, turn 2 contains/len, turn 3 IntoIterator.

task_spec.prompt: Implement `push_front(&mut self, value: T)` and `pop_front(&mut self) -> Option<T>` in `src/lib.rs`. push_front: create a new Node, set its `next` to the current head, set head to Some(Box::new(node)), increment len. pop_front: take head, set head to node.next, decrement len, return Some(node.value). Run `cargo test --quiet`.
followup_prompts: Good. Now implement `contains(&self, value: &T) -> bool` — traverse the linked list from head, comparing each node's value to the target using PartialEq. Also make sure `len()` and `is_empty()` work correctly (they use self.len which you should be maintaining). Run `cargo test --quiet` and fix any failures.

Final step: implement `into_iter(self)` in the `IntoIterator` impl — return `IntoIter { list: self }`. The `Iterator` impl for `IntoIter` already calls `pop_front()`. Run `cargo test --quiet` — all 4 tests must pass.
success_criteria: push_front adds to front, pop_front removes from front
len() is maintained correctly across push/pop
contains() traverses the list to find values
into_iter() allows collecting list into Vec
